title.en: Axisymmetric coil Green geometry and elliptic modulus

summary: Compute the source-offset radius, elliptic modulus squared, and distance used by the filament-coil Green expression.

identity.direction: observation point and coil centers to regularized Green geometry
identity.definition: Apply the fixed 1e-8 m observation-radius offset and compute m and the distance denominator elementwise.
identity.model: Scalar observation geometry for aligned circular coils.
identity.geometry: One observation point paired with one-dimensional coil-center arrays.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; modulus squared dimensionless.
identity.boundary: Raw observation radius must be nonnegative; underflow, overflow, and nonfinite geometry raise ValueError.
assumptions: All coil vectors have one-dimensional matching shapes.
The offset is applied exactly once before the response operator.

inputs.name: observation_radius_m
inputs.description: Raw cylindrical radius of the observation point.
inputs.constraints: Finite; must be nonnegative (a raw radius in (-1e-8, 0) is rejected: the source offset would silently regularize it to a positive one -- registered hardening); the regularized radius must be finite and positive.

inputs.name: observation_z_m
inputs.description: Axial coordinate of the observation point.

inputs.name: coil_radius_m
inputs.constraints: Finite 1-D with strictly positive entries, same shape as coil_z_m.

outputs.name: regularized_radius_m
outputs.description: Observation radius after the source axis offset, the value downstream GSEQ Green operators must receive.
outputs.constraints: Finite and positive; paired once with the response operator (which does not offset again).

outputs.name: modulus_squared
outputs.description: Per-coil squared elliptic modulus m = k^2.
outputs.constraints: Finite values in (0, 1] on accepted non-singular geometry; overflow from finite but extreme inputs raises ValueError (registered hardening); exactly 1 marks an observation point on the filament ring (singular downstream). A zero modulus caused by floating-point underflow raises ValueError.

outputs.name: distance_m
outputs.description: Per-coil Green geometric distance denominator sqrt((r0+rl)^2+(z0-zl)^2).

preconditions: All coil vectors have one-dimensional matching shapes.
supported: Finite paired coil arrays, the axis offset, endpoint modulus values, and declared overflow/underflow failures.
excluded: Coil-field evaluation, singular response handling, and arbitrary overflow behavior beyond the validated float64 domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for nonfinite, negative, mismatched, nonpositive-radius, underflowed, or overflowed geometry.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No iterative runtime failure is defined; NumPy floating-point failures are converted to ValueError by validation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is direct geometry arithmetic.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No geometry tuple is returned after validation failure.

example.description: Compute regularized geometry for one observation point and two coils.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus
radius, modulus, distance = compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus(
    0.3, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]))
assert radius == 0.3 + 1e-8
assert np.all((modulus > 0.0) & (modulus <= 1.0))
assert np.all(distance > 0.0)
example.expected: The returned radius is 0.30000001 m; both modulus-squared values are in (0,1] and distances are positive.

scope: Source-regularized geometry quantities against an independent recomputation.
A finite extreme geometry with an underflowed modulus is rejected before the Green response.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests establish the regularized radius, per-coil moduli and distance denominators against an independent recomputation (exact float equality on the offset, rtol=1e-15 on the closed forms), the (0, 1] modulus range on admissible geometry, axis-point admissibility through the source offset, and the fail-closed input contracts. No test establishes the geometry against an external physics reference; the relation is a direct closed-form contract of the saved source. The extreme underflow regression establishes rejection of one finite positive geometry whose computed modulus rounds to zero.
known_limitations: The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.
Registered input hardening: raw observation radii in (-1e-8, 0) are rejected rather than silently regularized to positive values by the source axis offset.

Registered output hardening: finite but extreme input magnitudes (e.g. r0 = rl = 1e308) that overflow the squared geometry sums are rejected with ValueError instead of handing non-finite modulus/distance downstream (the saved implementation returns them silently).
A modulus of exactly 1 (observation point on a filament ring) is an admissible output; consumers must reject it (the response operator does).
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
A zero modulus caused by floating-point underflow is rejected here; this is an additional SciRel boundary beyond the saved package.
